title: Truckers Strike Paralyzes Brazil for Ten Days
reason: Independent corroboration (Forbes, non-Wikipedia) confirms a nationwide Brazilian truckers strike in May 2018 lasting approximately 8-10 days, triggered by diesel price hikes under President Temer. It caused widespread shortages (food, fuel/aircraft fuel, animal feed, propane), a 28% YoY drop in retail revenue, and a 60% decline at gas stations. The Temer administration responded with major concessions: a 60-day diesel price cut, price caps, and fuel tax reductions — matching 'government capitulated to most demands' and exposing political vulnerability (Petrobras CEO resigned amid the crisis). Additional corroboration from a general web search also surfaced CNN, USDA/FAS, and an academic Systems Research and Behavioral Science paper all describing the same 10-day May 2018 strike, though CNN itself returned HTTP 451 on fetch. All material details (country=Brazil, year=2018, duration=~10 days, cause=diesel prices, consequences=shortages, government capitulation) align with the event description.
